app.tagline: Build the defensibility of your project — Helmer-style

hero.title: Is your moat a Power, or just a head-start?
hero.subtitle: Helmer: Power = Benefit + Barrier. Without a Barrier, the next well-funded competitor will arbitrage you away. 7Powers stress-tests your defensibility in 90 minutes, by sector and by stage. No workshop. No consultant.

how.heading: How it works
how.subheading: Five steps. The same method as Helmer workshops, without the 8-hour meeting.

1.title: Project setup
1.body: Sector, S-Curve stage, description. Questions and examples adapt to your context.

2.title: Market sizing
2.body: TAM / SAM / SOM + sources. 0-100 attractiveness score computed from the 'Value = Market × Power' logic.

3.title: 7 Powers self-assessment
3.body: One module per Power. Five questions Q1-Q5 each, Helmer's multiplicative scoring (zero on Benefit OR Barrier = no Power).

4.title: Power Map
4.body: Visual radar on the 7 axes. Top 3 Powers identified, red flags surfaced, global Defensibility Score.

5.title: Action plan
5.body: Three concrete next-steps per Power. PDF export for board, investors, or your team.

for.heading: Who it's for
for.subheading: Built for founders who pitch their moat without a framework, and programs that want a structured deliverable.

defi.title: DeFi / Web3 founders
defi.body: You pitch a protocol as your moat, but without an identified Power it's just an arbitrable advantage. Liquidity ≠ Network Effects. TVL ≠ Switching Costs.

ai.title: AI / Agents founders
ai.body: Against LLM providers, your Power probably isn't your model. Cornered Resource (exclusive data)? Counter-Positioning (business model incumbents can't copy)?

incubator.title: Programs / Incubators
incubator.body: A structured post-workshop deliverable: Power Map + action plan for each project in your cohort. Comparable across projects.

powersGrid.heading: The 7 Powers of Helmer
powersGrid.subheading: Each Power = a specific mechanism for durable defensibility. Most projects only have 2-3, and that's normal.

power.actionItemsHint: Concrete, actionable, within the next 90 days. Leave blank what you haven't defined yet.
power.benefitHint: Describe in one or two sentences the concrete cash-flow benefit. Not a slogan — a number or a mechanism.
power.barrierHint: Why does an identical, well-funded competitor fail to arbitrage your Benefit? This is what turns an advantage into a Power.

scoreBands.strong: Solid Power. You have a real moat on this axis.
scoreBands.solid: Credible but perfectible. Strengthen the Barrier.
scoreBands.weak: Embryonic or arguable Power. Either the project is young, or this isn't really a Power.
scoreBands.absent: No Power detected on this axis — that's OK, you don't need all 7.

scale.tagline: Unit costs drop as volume rises. Competitor must scale up to match.
scale.definition: When your unit costs fall with volume, your price beats smaller competitors. The Benefit is measurable. The Barrier comes from the fact that a challenger would need to reach YOUR volume — which takes years and capital — to match your costs.

examples.defi: Uniswap V3: massive TVL → better routing pricing → more TVL. Smaller Curve / Balancer offer less competitive spreads on major pairs. A competitor must attract billions in liquidity to match — takes years.
examples.ai: Anthropic / OpenAI: training cost amortized across millions of users. Marginal inference cost drops with optimizations on shared GPU pools. A new lab must absorb CapEx infra ($100M+) before matching unit economics.
examples.saas: AWS: cost per compute-hour drops drastically with the scale of their data centers and hardware procurement. GCP / Azure took 10+ years to approach comparable unit economics on certain services.
examples.web3-other: Layer 2 networks (Arbitrum, Optimism): more TPS = lower cost per tx via rollup batching. A new L2 must attract volume before having competitive costs.

q1.label: Is the unit-cost benefit quantifiable?
q1.hint: Can you give a number: 'at 10x our volume, our cost per X drops by Y%'?

q2.label: Is the economic impact significant at your stage?
q2.hint: Does the cost drop give you a price edge > 10% that competitors can't match?

q3.label: How much time / capital for a competitor to catch up?
q3.hint: Order of magnitude: 6 months? 3 years? $10M? $500M? The longer and more expensive, the higher the Barrier.

q4.label: Would an identical competitor with $50M fail to match your volume quickly?
q4.hint: 'Me too won't do' test. If yes (they would fail), the Barrier holds. If no, it's just an arbitrable head-start.

q5.label: Are you at the Takeoff stage where Scale Economies are built?
q5.hint: Scale Economies are built at the Takeoff stage (PMF achieved, scaling up). At Origination it's too early; at Stability it's locked in.

scale.benefitPlaceholder: e.g. At $1B TVL, our slippage is 30% lower than top-5 competitor AMMs.
scale.barrierPlaceholder: e.g. A challenger must drain ~$500M TVL over 12-18 months and pay liquidity-mining incentives (~$5M/yr) to match.

actionPlaceholders.0: Precisely measure unit-cost gap vs. top 3 competitors
actionPlaceholders.1: Publicly document unit economics to signal the Barrier
actionPlaceholders.2: Accelerate volume acquisition on the steepest segment of the curve

network.tagline: Value grows for every user when more users join. A competitor must reach critical mass.
network.definition: When each new user increases value for existing ones, your service gets better as it grows. The Benefit is measurable (engagement, retention). The Barrier is the chicken-and-egg problem: a competitor must acquire enough users to offer the same value — which costs heavy incentives and takes time.

examples.defi: Uniswap: more LPs → more liquidity → better pricing → more traders → more fees for LPs. Aave / Compound: more lenders → better rates → more borrowers. Virtuous loop a competitor must kickstart with massive incentives (gas wars / liquidity mining wars).
examples.ai: Cursor / GitHub Copilot: more users → more feedback signals → better model → more users. Agent marketplaces (LangChain hub, OpenAI GPT store): more devs publish → more variety → more users → more incentive to publish.
examples.saas: Linear: connected teams generate cross-team network. Notion: shared workspace becomes the organization's hub. Figma: shared design files become the common asset. A 10x-better competitor struggles if the network has taken hold.
examples.web3-other: Lens / Farcaster: onchain social graph. Wallets (Phantom, MetaMask): adopted standards. NFT marketplaces (OpenSea, eroded by Blur). Competitor must do costly mass-onboarding to match the critical mass.

q1.label: Is the marginal-value-per-additional-user effect quantifiable?
q1.hint: Can you measure: 'at 10x users, utility per user rises by X%' (metric: engagement, retention, ARPU)?

q2.label: Is the network effect already active in your current metrics?
q2.hint: Non-linear effect visible: churn drops with scale, ARPU rises, CAC falls.

q3.label: How many users must a competitor acquire to reach your value-per-user?
q3.hint: Orders: 100K? 1M? 10M? The higher the threshold, the more solid the Barrier.

q4.label: Would a competitor with $50M marketing budget succeed in poaching your users via incentives?
q4.hint: Me-too-won't-do test. If no (network holds), Barrier solid. If yes (gas wars work), it's arbitrable.

q5.label: Are you at the Takeoff stage where Network Effects are built?
q5.hint: Takeoff (PMF + scaling) — ideal moment. Origination = too early, Stability = should already be locked.

network.benefitPlaceholder: e.g. At 100K active users, our engagement/user has doubled vs 10K. Churn dropped from 8% to 3%.
network.barrierPlaceholder: e.g. A competitor must acquire 50K active users (~$5M CAC) to offer the same engagement — ~18 months of paid acquisition.

actionPlaceholders.0: Identify the precise network KPI (engagement, retention, per-user ARPU) and track it monthly
actionPlaceholders.1: Reduce CAC on the segment where the network self-reinforces fastest
actionPlaceholders.2: Lock down a network primitive (data format, integration) competitors can't easily replicate

counter.tagline: A business model incumbents can't copy without cannibalizing themselves.
counter.definition: You adopt a fundamentally different economic model that gives you an edge. The Benefit is measurable (lower price, better margins, different distribution). The Barrier is NOT technical — it's cannibalization: if the incumbent copies you, they destroy their own existing business.

examples.defi: Aave / Compound vs banks: 4-8% APY on stablecoins when banks offer 0.1%. A bank can't match without cannibalizing its free checking accounts and interest spread. MakerDAO: programmable over-collateralization no one copies without rethinking their entire credit back office.
examples.ai: Cursor vs JetBrains: pay-per-completion + AI-first vs annual license + plugin. JetBrains can't drop the license without crashing its recurring revenue. Open-source LLMs (Mistral, Llama): Anthropic can't open-source Claude without killing its API revenue.
examples.saas: Linear vs Jira: no enterprise sales, transparent pricing, no heavy admin. Atlassian can't match without destroying its sales-led business. Notion vs MS Office: freemium + native collaboration, Microsoft must protect Office 365 enterprise.
examples.web3-other: DAO governance vs corporate structure: token-voted, open, transparent. A corp can't tokenize governance without SEC headaches. Bitcoin self-custody vs custodial banks: a bank can't offer self-custody without blowing up its custodian model.

q1.label: Is your economic model fundamentally different from incumbents (not just better, different)?
q1.hint: Pricing model, distribution, business unit, monetization — where is the structural delta?

q2.label: Is the value differential strong enough for a user to switch from an incumbent?
q2.hint: Does the low price or superior offering compensate for switch friction (trust, data, habits)?

q3.label: If an incumbent tried to copy you, what exactly would they have to cannibalize?
q3.hint: Name the concrete revenue stream of the incumbent that disappears if they adopt your model.

q4.label: Would a competitor with $50M adopting your model face the same cannibalization dilemma as incumbents?
q4.hint: If a newcomer (no legacy) can copy you painlessly, your Power is arbitrable. If every entrant must make the same choice, Barrier solid.

q5.label: Are you at Origination where Counter-Positioning is built?
q5.hint: Origination (pre-PMF) — ideal moment to design a disruptive model. Takeoff = too late to pivot the model.

counter.benefitPlaceholder: e.g. Our usage-based pricing cuts cost for 80% of users by 60% vs incumbent seat-based pricing.
counter.barrierPlaceholder: e.g. Jira can't adopt our usage pricing without cannibalizing ~$2B of enterprise revenue locked in annual contracts.

actionPlaceholders.0: Articulate in writing the exact cannibalization dilemma each incumbent faces vs your model
actionPlaceholders.1: Lock in the value differential while incumbents can't respond
actionPlaceholders.2: Identify the most exposed incumbent segment and accelerate acquisition there

switching.tagline: A switch cost for users that lets you capture a premium or hold against 10x-better competitors.
switching.definition: Once a user adopts your product, the cost to leave becomes significant (time, data, retraining, broken integrations). You can price at a premium as long as that cost > a competitor's value delta. The Barrier grows with usage — every additional month reinforces lock-in.

examples.defi: Aave / Compound: LP positions, locked governance tokens (veCRV at Curve), onchain reputation. Switching = unwind positions, lose accrued rewards, redo KYC elsewhere. veCRV: 4-year lock for max voting power = massive switching cost.
examples.ai: Cursor / Claude Projects: personalized agent on your code style and docs, refined prompts/workflows. ChatGPT memory: the AI knows your preferences. Switching = start from scratch, lose weeks of tuning.
examples.saas: Salesforce: CRM integrations with 50+ tools, historical client data, automated workflows. Notion: workspace, templates, integrations. Switching = loss of structured data + weeks of migration.
examples.web3-other: ENS names: your .eth identity. NFT collections: community-anchored social status. Wallet: seed phrase + accumulated onchain reputation.

q1.label: Is the user's switch cost quantifiable (hours, $ migration, data lost)?
q1.hint: How long + how much $ would an average user need to migrate to a competitor?

q2.label: Is the premium price (or retention) this cost lets you capture significant?
q2.hint: Can you price 15%+ above equivalent competitors without losing users? That's the signal.

q3.label: How much time / effort does a user invest to switch after 6 months with you?
q3.hint: The longer the tenure, the higher the cost (accumulated data). Estimate for 1 month and 1 year of use.

q4.label: If a free + 2x-better competitor showed up tomorrow, would your active users stay?
q4.hint: Ultimate test. If yes (low Switching Costs), it's not a Power. If no, solid Barrier.

q5.label: Are you at Takeoff stage where Switching Costs accumulate through usage?
q5.hint: Takeoff (PMF + scale) — every month of usage per cohort adds switching cost. Origination = too early, Stability = saturated.

switching.benefitPlaceholder: e.g. Our users average 50+ active integrations after 12 months. Migration takes 3-6 months of data engineering work.
switching.barrierPlaceholder: e.g. A competitor must not only match our product but also rebuild integrations with the 50+ tools our users connect — ~$100k+ per client.

actionPlaceholders.0: Measure concrete switch cost (time, $, lost data) for your average user and surface it
actionPlaceholders.1: Add features that grow user investment (custom templates, integrations, accumulated data)
actionPlaceholders.2: Raise switching costs specifically on segments most at risk of churn

branding.tagline: A brand that commands a price premium through perception, built on years of consistent signaling.
branding.definition: Your brand evokes quality, security, or status in a way that justifies a price above the objectively equivalent. The Benefit is measurable (price premium, conversion on brand name). The Barrier is hysteresis: it takes 3-5+ years of investment and consistency for a brand to settle in — a competitor can't shortcut that time.

examples.defi: Aave / MakerDAO: 'blue-chip DeFi'. Even if a new lending protocol offers 1% better, whales stay out of trust. Chainlink: the reference oracle — a new oracle, even technically superior, struggles to match accumulated trust.
examples.ai: Anthropic Claude: recognized safety-first positioning. Midjourney: premium artist brand. Against LLM commoditization, models work nearly the same — the brand makes the difference at the buying decision.
examples.saas: Stripe: developer trust. Notion: cool-kids productivity. Linear: engineering elegance. 30-50% price premium vs functionally equivalent competitors (Square, Coda, Jira).
examples.web3-other: BAYC: social status. Crypto.com: mass-market trust. Coinbase: the 'safe' platform (US regulation). Brand wins over tech in contexts where trust is scarce.

q1.label: Does your brand command a measurable price premium vs equivalent alternatives?
q1.hint: Cite the delta: 'Our product prices at X, equivalent competitor at Y, and users still pay'.

q2.label: Is the 3+ years of brand investment significant and consistent?
q2.hint: Content, design, partnerships, comm presence — what cumulative $ + consistency?

q3.label: How many years + marketing spend must a competitor invest to match your perception?
q3.hint: Brand = hysteresis. Orders: 3 years + $5M? 7 years + $50M? A mature brand takes decades.

q4.label: Would a functionally identical competitor with $50M marketing fail to match your brand in 2 years?
q4.hint: That's the speed of hysteresis. If yes (slow), Barrier solid. If $50M commoditizes you in 2 years, that's not Branding.

q5.label: Are you at Stability stage where Branding consolidates?
q5.hint: Stability (PMF + maturity) — that's when Branding really settles. Origination = too early (nascent brand), Takeoff = under construction.

branding.benefitPlaceholder: e.g. Our conversion on name-search is 4x higher than category-search. Clients cite our brand in 60% of RFPs.
branding.barrierPlaceholder: e.g. Our brand was built through 6 years of content investing (~$3M spent), exclusive partnerships, 70+ NPS. A competitor must reproduce this time + capital + accumulated trust.

actionPlaceholders.0: Measure the real price premium vs equivalent competitors (controlled comparison)
actionPlaceholders.1: Invest in the most distinctive quality signal for your segment (security, design, engineering, tone)
actionPlaceholders.2: Protect the brand on its cardinal points — a brand miss costs 10x more to fix than to avoid

cornered.tagline: Exclusive, durable access to a critical asset — data, IP, contract, talent, distribution.
cornered.definition: You hold an asset others don't and can't have: contractual exclusivity, intellectual property, proprietary dataset, top talent. Without that asset, your product would be commodity. The Barrier is legal or structural (ownership), not competitive (skill).

examples.defi: Ondo Finance: RWA partnership with BlackRock (BUIDL). A competitor can't have the same exclusive partnership. Anchorage Digital: regulated US custody license. Circle (USDC): US banking rails locked through 8+ years of compliance work.
examples.ai: Bloomberg: proprietary financial dataset to train a finance LLM. Hollywood studios: signed video data for video models. NVIDIA: CUDA + dev ecosystem locked. xAI / OpenAI: top ML talent retained via equity + IP restrictions.
examples.saas: Palantir: classified government contracts (DoD, NSA) — non-replicable without clearance. LinkedIn: data scraping agreements + lawsuits vs imitators. Salesforce: decades of proprietary CRM client data.
examples.web3-other: ENS: premium .eth domain names finite (never more). Cryptography patents (zkSync, StarkWare). Binance / Coinbase exclusive first-listing agreements.

q1.label: Is the asset truly exclusive (verifiable, defensible contract / IP / patent)?
q1.hint: Is it legally or structurally verifiable, not just a 'head-start'?

q2.label: Is this asset critical to the business — without it, value collapses?
q2.hint: If you lost the asset tomorrow (contract broken, IP invalidated), how much value would you lose?

q3.label: What would it take for a competitor to acquire an equivalent asset?
q3.hint: Orders: $1M? $100M? Acquisition of another company? Truly one-of-a-kind?

q4.label: Could a $50M competitor buy or license an equivalent asset?
q4.hint: Decisive test. If yes, your asset isn't cornered, just expensive. If no (truly unique), Barrier ironclad.

q5.label: Are you at Origination where Cornered Resource is won?
q5.hint: Origination — moment to win exclusivity (partnerships, IP, key hires). Takeoff = the window closes, Stability = too late.

cornered.benefitPlaceholder: e.g. Our proprietary dataset covers 80% of historical corporate bond trades, accumulated via 8 exclusive bank partnerships.
cornered.barrierPlaceholder: e.g. The 8 partnerships are each 5-year terms, signed in 2024, with exclusivity clauses. A competitor must wait until 2029 to propose an equivalent deal — and must sign them blind.

actionPlaceholders.0: Lock down the most strategic exclusivities legally (IP audit, NDA, non-circumvent clauses)
actionPlaceholders.1: Identify top talent whose loss would be fatal and protect them (equity, terms)
actionPlaceholders.2: Build a 2nd-order moat around the asset (workflow, data architecture that makes the asset more useful at your shop than elsewhere)

process.tagline: Operational excellence — a complex process, accumulated over years, that a competitor can't replicate by reading a book.
process.definition: Your organization has developed an operational process — quality, speed, cost — that beats competitors and that no one can copy by reading documentation. It takes years of learning by mistakes, refinement, and cultural embedding. The Barrier is tacit complexity.

examples.defi: Aave: risk management refined by 4+ years of stress tests (oracle architecture, risk weight parameterization, liquidation engine). Curve: veCRV design and incentive structure so complex that forks (Convex included) break on the details.
examples.ai: Anthropic: constitutional AI methodology, refined RLHF process. OpenAI: proprietary eval harness, fine-tuning pipeline. Tesla: self-driving training data pipeline (millions-of-miles fleet) + Dojo training infra. The open-sourced model doesn't capture the process that produced it.
examples.saas: AWS: data-center ops at massive scale, 20 years of experience. Toyota Production System: book published 30 years ago, no one copies it fully. Salesforce: refined sales + customer success machine.
examples.web3-other: Ethereum validators: 10 years of incremental decentralization (Geth, Erigon, multi-client). Cosmos / Polkadot: years-deep cross-chain coordination process.

q1.label: Is your operational process measurably superior (cost/quality/speed) to competitors?
q1.hint: Cite the metric: 'Our X cost is Y% lower', 'Our cycle time is Z min vs W min'.

q2.label: Is the performance gap vs competitors significant (>20%)?
q2.hint: 10% is noise. 20%+ is a potential Power. 50%+ is locked in.

q3.label: How many years must a competitor invest to replicate the process?
q3.hint: Process Power = tacit knowledge. Estimate: 2 years with a senior poach? 5 years from scratch?

q4.label: Would a competitor copy-pasting your full playbook fail to match your operational results?
q4.hint: Decisive test. If even with full docs they can't, it's real Process Power (Toyota, Aave). If docs suffice, it's arbitrable.

q5.label: Are you at Stability stage where Process Power consolidates?
q5.hint: Stability — the org has lived complete cycles, refined processes, accumulated lessons. Origination/Takeoff = too early to have depth.

process.benefitPlaceholder: e.g. Our deploy time for a new feature is 4 days vs ~3 weeks at direct competitors. Defect rate 0.2% vs 1-2% industry standard.
process.barrierPlaceholder: e.g. Our process rests on 6 years of iteration across 3 layers (architecture, tooling, engineering culture). A competitor poaching our VP Eng would take 2-3 years to replicate — the process is distributed across 30 people, not centralized.

actionPlaceholders.0: Document the key process internally (but protect sensitive details — avoid IP leakage)
actionPlaceholders.1: Measure the performance gap vs competitors on 2-3 key metrics and publish in marketing
actionPlaceholders.2: Strengthen tacit-process transmission (mentorship, systematic post-mortems, engineering culture)

module1.title: Market sizing
module1.subtitle: Helmer: Value = Market × Power. No market, no value — even with a Power. Three numbers + your sources.

scoreBands.strong: Solid market. A real Power on top of this gives genuine defensibility.
scoreBands.solid: Viable market. Question is whether your SOM holds up.
scoreBands.thin: Thin market. Verify that your angle is worth the effort.
scoreBands.empty: Not yet sized. Start with at least TAM.

module1.coherenceWarningBody: TAM should be ≥ SAM ≥ SOM. You can still save, but it signals to readers that the numbers warrant a second look.
module1.tamHint: If everyone on Earth used your product, how much is it worth? The theoretical ceiling.
module1.samHint: The portion of TAM you can realistically reach (geography, segment, channel).
module1.somHint: What you can concretely capture in 3-5 years. Resist the temptation to inflate.
module1.sourcesHint: One per line. Analyst reports, public stats, proprietary market data.
module1.sourcesPlaceholder:
Statista Crypto Industry Report 2025
Messari State of DeFi Q1 2026
…
module1.notesPlaceholder: How you built these numbers (top-down, bottom-up, comparable, etc.)

module0.title: The project
module0.subtitle: Lay the foundation. Name, sector, stage. These are the three axes we'll stress-test your moat against.
module0.sectorHint: Determines which Power examples we'll surface.
module0.stageHint: Helmer: each Power is built at a different stage. We tune the questions accordingly.
module0.descriptionPlaceholder: One or two sentences to set the scene.

sectors.aiHint: LLM apps, agent platforms, AI infra.
sectors.saasHint: Classic Helmer cases. Linear, Notion, Stripe.

synthesis.title: Power Map & Synthesis
synthesis.subtitle: Overview of your defensibility. The radar shows your 7 axes, the global score combines top 3 Powers and market attractiveness, red flags surface fragile claims.
synthesis.emptyBody: Fill at least one Power module to see your Power Map build up. The radar and Defensibility Score compute in real time from your assessments.
synthesis.radarAriaLabel: 7-axis radar representing the project's Power scores

breakdown.formulaNote: Adapted Helmer formula: Defensibility = (Top 3 Powers × 0.7) + (Market × 0.3). We don't average all 7 — Helmer says most projects have 2-3 Powers, not 7.

scoreBands.strong: Strong defensibility. You have a real moat on 2-3 axes aligned with a viable market.
scoreBands.solid: Credible defensibility. A few Powers well identified, consolidation still needed.
scoreBands.weak: Fragile defensibility. Either the project is young, or the claimed Powers are arbitrable.
scoreBands.absent: No clear defensibility. To Helmer, this means risk of arbitrage by the next well-funded competitor.
scoreBands.notReady: Fill at least one Power to compute the score.

synthesis.topPowersSubtitle: Your highest-scoring Powers. The #1 is shown in gold — that's your primary moat.
synthesis.redFlagsSubtitle: Inconsistencies detected between your claims and Helmer's methodology. Not blocking — but worth a look.

stageMismatch.title: {power} off-stage
stageMismatch.body: You're claiming {power} but this Power usually builds at a different S-Curve stage. Branding at Origination = impossible (hysteresis takes 3-5 years). Scale at Origination = too early (pre-PMF). Re-check the stage.

unarticulated.title: {power} unarticulated
unarticulated.body: You scored >40 on {power} but didn't describe the Benefit or Barrier in plain words. A Power without articulation is just a slogan. Fill the textareas to make it credible.

maxScore.title: {power} maxed on every axis
maxScore.body: Q1 through Q5 all at 5 on {power} — that's suspicious. Helmer's methodology is skeptical by default: if everything is perfect, either the project is exceptional, or you're overclaiming. Re-challenge Q3 (Barrier height) in particular.

tooManyPowers.title: Too many Powers claimed
tooManyPowers.body: You have 5+ Powers above 60/100. Helmer is clear: most enduring businesses have 2-3 Powers, not 7. Likely overclaim — re-challenge the weakest ones.

noClearMoat.title: No dominant Power
noClearMoat.body: No Power above 50/100. Per Helmer, without a clear Power, your project will be arbitraged as soon as a well-funded competitor shows up. Either the project is still young, or you need to dig for a better angle.

thinMarket.title: Thin market + strong Powers
thinMarket.body: Value = Market × Power. You have Powers but your market attractiveness score is below 30/100. Even a strong Power on a micro-market yields micro-value. Re-evaluate your SAM/SOM.

synthesis.stageFitSubtitle: Your project is at the {stage} stage. Each Power builds at a different stage per Helmer — here's whether your claims align.
